newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler says March sales may dip slightly.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler says March sales may dip slightly.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chairman Robert Eaton said Wednesday the automaker's March U.S. car and truck sales may be down slightly from a year ago because of a slow start to the traditional spring selling season.
"The spring selling season hasn't really yet gotten underway so it's likely they'll be down a little bit," Eaton said of Chrysler's sales for March.

Speaking to reporters at the New York Auto Show, Eaton also said he does not believe the Federal Reserve Board's 25-basis-point increase in the federal funds rate on Tuesday will hurt U.S. auto sales.
"We expected the quarter point (increase). We're not unhappy in any way, shape or form with it," Eaton said, adding, "We think (Fed Charman Alan) Greenspan has done a heck of a good job."

Martin Levine, the general manager for the Chrysler Plymouth Jeep Eagle Division, said the "pre-production build process" for the new Prowler roadster is taking longer than expected, and may push back the originally planned Spring 1997 debut for the cars.

Chrysler executives said work on the new aluminum body panels used by the car is taking longer than expected, and the company wants to make sure the car is of top quality before it is released to dealers.
"There is not a problem with the Prowler," Eaton said. The car is a bold experiment for Chrysler into aluminum car construction and is being touted as the premier image car for the Plymouth brand.
He added that he will personally drive pre-production Prowlers within the next two weeks and the company could make a decision at that time on when to start volume production.
Both Eaton and Levine refused to speculate on when that production would begin.
"This car is so important for us that unless it's perfect, it's not going anywhere," Levine said.
